problem: Off-the-shelf VLAs (e.g. Pi0.5) struggle on the long-horizon, bimanual, mobile household tasks of the BEHAVIOR Challenge: compounding errors, visually ambiguous non-Markovian states, no recovery demonstrations, and multi-modal actions.
motivation: BEHAVIOR-1K requires 50 long-horizon tasks (avg 6.6 min) with one policy and successful-only teleoperated demos, so any deviation leads to out-of-distribution states and the policy freezes. The authors address these failure modes with modeling of action structure, stage context, and heuristics from failure analysis.
key_idea: Adapt Pi0.5 to BEHAVIOR with correlated-noise flow matching (plus correlation-aware inpainting), System 2 stage tracking, learnable mixed-layer attention, multi-sample flow matching, action compression and gripper correction rules.
insight: The authors provide almost no formal ablations, so the causal evidence is thin. The one clear ablation is that the gripper-open correction rule raised q-score 2.2x on 13 tasks (39 episodes). Qualitatively, multi-task training over 50 tasks produced emergent recovery behaviors (e.g. picking up fallen objects) absent in single-task models, and pretrained Pi0.5 weights were essential (small from-scratch models failed). Training was under-converged (~2 epochs), which suggests compute was the main limit.
method: Correlated noise flow matching: sample noise from N(0, βΣ+(1-β)I) with Σ the empirical 30x23 action correlation matrix (β=0.5, Cholesky), so the noisiest denoising steps already have action structure.

Correlation-aware soft inpainting: rolling window predicts 30 actions, executes 26, keeps the last 4 as constraints; corrections on constrained dims are propagated to free dims via Σ_UO Σ_OO^-1, applied only for t>0.3.

System 2 stage tracking: linear stage classifier on VLM output (5-15 stages/task), majority voting over 3 predictions (forward, skip, rollback rules), fused with task embedding into 5 task/stage tokens.
Learnable mixed-layer attention: each action-expert layer attends to learned linear combinations (scalar weights + bias) of all VLM layers' K/V, initialized to identity.
Task embeddings and custom masks: 50 trainable 2048-d task embeddings replace text; hierarchical attention mask isolates images/task from noisy state/stage tokens; FAST auxiliary loss (weight 0.05).

Training: multi-sample flow matching (15 (t,ε) samples per VLM pass), delta actions with per-timestamp normalization, multi-task pretraining (15 days on 8xH200) then fine-tuning in 3 task groups (4 checkpoints in total).

Inference tricks: cubic-spline action compression 26→20 steps (1.3x speedup, disabled near gripper changes, base velocity scaled 1.3x) and rule-based gripper opening on implausible closures, plus one radio-task rule.

setting.backbone: Pi0.5 (PaliGemma VLM with SigLIP-So400m + 300M Gemma action expert), fine-tuned
setting.training_data: BEHAVIOR-1K challenge demonstrations: 10,000 teleoperated expert demos over 50 tasks (1200+ hours); initialized from pretrained Pi0.5 weights
setting.observation: RGB 224x224 from head and two wrist cameras + proprioceptive state
setting.action_space: 23-D continuous (3D base velocity, 4D trunk, 2x7 arm joints, 2 grippers), delta joint actions, chunk of 30

numbers.eval_set_note: private held-out leaderboard: 10 held-out instances per task x 50 tasks
numbers.extra: multi-task pretraining then task-group fine-tuning; correction rules; action compression
numbers.evidence: Table 1: rank 1, Binary Success private 0.1240, q_score private 0.2599

numbers.eval_set_note: public leaderboard: 10 published instances per task x 50 tasks
numbers.evidence: Table 1: rank 1, Binary Success public 0.1120, q_score public 0.2605

numbers_note: Success rates are printed as fractions (0.xxxx) and kept as printed. Only leaderboard numbers are given; ablations are mostly qualitative, except the gripper-rule 2.2x q-score gain on 39 episodes.
results: 1st place in the 2025 BEHAVIOR Challenge with q-score 0.2599 private / 0.2605 public and binary success 0.1240 private. The runner-up Comet (NVIDIA) scored 0.2514 private q-score (0.1140 binary success) and third place scored 0.1591.
limitations: No systematic ablations, so the contribution of each proposed component (correlated noise, mixed-layer attention, stage tracking) is unverified
Models under-trained (~2 epochs) and rely on competition-specific heuristics (gripper/radio rules) and task-specific checkpoints; success stays low (~12% binary)
Training on only successful, idealized demos with no recovery data; dexterity failures dominate
